questions.question: A class defines `bank = "SkillPrep Bank"` at class level. After `a.bank = "Other Bank"` on one instance, what does another instance `b.bank` return?
options: "Other Bank", because class attributes are shared
"SkillPrep Bank", because the assignment created an instance attribute only on a
questions.explanation: Assigning through an instance always creates or updates an attribute in that instance's __dict__. The class attribute is untouched, so b still finds it on the class.

questions.question: Why does `members = []` defined at class level cause a bug when instances call `self.members.append(...)`?
options: Lists cannot be class attributes in Python
All instances share the same list object, so appending through one instance is visible from every other
append raises an error on class attributes
Each instance gets a copy, so the appended values are lost
questions.explanation: append mutates the existing object found via lookup on the class rather than rebinding a name, so every instance sees the same shared list. Create the list in __init__ instead.

questions.question: Which statement about `@classmethod` and `@staticmethod` is correct?
options: A classmethod receives the class as its first argument, making it suitable for alternative constructors; a staticmethod receives no implicit first argument
A staticmethod receives the class, a classmethod receives the instance
Both receive self, but classmethods cannot be called on instances
They are identical; the names are just conventions
questions.explanation: A classmethod gets cls (the class or subclass it was called on), so cls(...) builds the right type. A staticmethod is a plain function namespaced in the class.

questions.question: What happens when you assign `p.z = 3` on an instance of a class with `__slots__ = ("x", "y")`?
options: z is silently stored in the instance __dict__
An AttributeError is raised because there is no slot or __dict__ for z
questions.explanation: __slots__ replaces the per-instance __dict__ with fixed storage for the listed names, so assigning any other attribute fails with AttributeError.
